answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the beacon checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The ferrous graph is rebuilt each epoch, thus the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the nebula audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 2 times its size, so a group of 62 keys loses far more than 62 single identities would. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
